Row.Text: Many Yields, especially those from Policies, Beliefs, and Buildings, state that they [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]''Scale with Era''[ENDCOLOR]. This means that, as the game progresses, indicated Yield values increase in a linear fashion based on the current Era:[NEWLINE]1x in the Ancient and Classical Eras.[NEWLINE]2x in the Medieval Era.[NEWLINE]3x in the Renaissance Era.[NEWLINE]4x in the Industrial Era.[NEWLINE]5x in the Modern Era.[NEWLINE]6x in the Atomic Era.[NEWLINE]7x in the Information Era.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In special cases like Korea, they may scale with Odd Era or skipping an era before scaling and follow a format based on the Current era like:[NEWLINE]1x in the Ancient/Classical Eras.[NEWLINE]2x in the Medieval/Renaissance Eras.[NEWLINE]3x in the Industrial/Modern Eras.[NEWLINE]4x in the Atomic/Information Eras.
What are Yields Scaling with Era?

City State Embassies are an additional method in Vox Populi to gain Delegates in the World Congress. To establish an Embassy in a City State, move a Great Diplomat to a land tile of the City State and select "Establish an Embassy". An Embassy grants 1 additional Delegate in the World Congress. In each City State, only one Embassy can be established by a Civilization, so be quick. When a Civilization is conquered, all of its City State Embassies are transferred to the conquering Civilization.

Historic Events represent monumental achievements that may occur during a game. These events require planning or user interaction, and are thus a dynamic part of acquiring cultural influence over other civilizations. When one of the following Historic Events is completed, receive a [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism boost with all known Civs based on your recent [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism output:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Earn a [ICON_GREAT_PEOPLE] Great Person[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Build a [ICON_WONDER] World Wonder[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Win a [ICON_WAR] War (Warscore 25+)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Enter a new [ICON_RESEARCH] Era[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Enter a [ICON_GOLDEN_AGE] Golden Age (Artistry)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Completing an [ICON_RES_ARTIFACTS] / [ICON_RES_HIDDEN_ARTIFACTS] Archaeological Dig (Artistry)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] [ICON_CARAVAN] Trade with a Major Civilization (Caravansary, etc)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] [ICON_CARGO_SHIP] Trade with a Major Civilization (Harbor, etc)[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] [ICON_CARAVAN]/[ICON_CARGO_SHIP] Trade with a [ICON_CITY_STATE] City-State (Policy Only)[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The amount of Tourism received by these events is based on your culture and tourism per turn over the past few turns. The value of this is also adjusted based on the number of cities in your empire and your tourism modifier with the target civ. Finally, the amount of tourism you receive is also modified by a few social policies and ideological tenets, as well as leader traits, buildings, and the number of cities in your empire.

Resistance is a mechanic through which Civilizations that have conquered one or more Capitals will find it increasingly difficult to capture additional Capitals. During combat, you may see the modifier [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Resistance (Domination)[ENDCOLOR] appear for you (a bonus) or for the enemy (a penalty). This modifier only appears after either you or your opponent have captured an enemy Capital. The modifier changes based on the number of foreign (non-City-State) Capitals owned and the number of foreign Capitals in total. The more Capitals captured by one player, the higher this penalty becomes!

If you choose to raze a City, there is a chance each turn that the City will spawn Partisans loyal to the Civilization you conquered this City from. These units will only spawn if you are still at war with the Civilization. If you are no longer at war, any spawned Partisans will be considered Barbarians. Be careful with aggressively razing enemy Cities, as the sudden appearance of Partisans could turn the tide against you!

War, war never changes. Well, actually, it does. As a war progresses, the citizens of your empire will become more and more aware of the dangers of prolonged conflict, and will begin to develop [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]War Weariness[ENDCOLOR]. War Weariness is calculated for each player based on three factors: the number of turns you've been at war with them, the amount of damage you've received from them, and half the amount of damage you've inflicted on them. This value is then compared to the current "power" of your units and cities to calculate a percentage (capped at 100%), and the highest % penalty from any player is applied to your empire. After capturing a city from a player, your War Weariness with that player will be suspended until two turns have passed, as your people hope for a favorable end of the war. If an AI leader is able but unwilling to make peace with a human player, that leader is also ignored.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In addition, making peace with another civilization will immediately halve your War Weariness with them, and liberating a city will reduce your War Weariness by 25% with all civilizations.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]War Weariness has three major effects:[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Unhappiness from War Weariness[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Increased Production and Gold costs for Military Units[NEWLINE][ICON_BULLET] Reduced maximum Military Unit Supply Cap[NEWLINE]Be careful of overextending during a single conflict!

The maximum number of Military Units you can field at any one time is called your Military Unit Supply Cap. This number, indicated on the Top Panel next to the [ICON_WAR] Symbol, increases based on two factors: the total population of all of your cities, and the number of buildings or policies you have that increase your Military Unit Supply Cap. Some buildings, such as the Barracks, increase your Supply Cap by a fixed amount. Others, like Walls, increase your Supply cap by a percentage of the city's population.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Military Unit Supply Cap increases from static elements, like Barracks, and percentage bonuses from population decline over time based on your empire's technological level. You will need more and more percentage bonuses to overcome this and field large armies![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]If, for any reason, you exceed your Military Unit Supply Cap, you will be penalized 5% Production and Food in all Cities (per unit over the cap).

Owned Forts and Citadels that are built next to a water tile count as Canals and can be accessed by your military ships. You can build Canals to connect Lakes (and Cities next to them) to the Ocean. It is not possible to have two adjacent Forts or two adjacent Citadels, but one Fort and one Citadel can be built next to each other. A City next to a Lake that is connected to the Ocean by a Canal can construct military ships (but not coastal buildings), and Canals can also be used by owned and foreign cargo ships.

You gain a new Spy whenever the number of [ICON_SPY_POINT] Spy Points exceeds the threshold (minimum: 100). The threshold value is reduced based on the number of Civilizations and City-States existing at the start of the game. When the first Civilization reaches Renaissance, or when you reach any later Era, you gain 100 [ICON_SPY_POINT] Spy Points. Some Buildings and Policies also provide [ICON_SPY_POINT] Spy Points.

The Local Happiness of a city is determined as follows:[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Some Happiness is generated locally by the City. This can be through Buildings, Policies, World Wonders or Worked Landmarks.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The total amount of Happiness coming from empire-wide sources (like Luxury Resources or allied City States) is distributed deck-of-cards style among all Cities. This is done automatically, prioritizing Cities that have less Local Happiness than Population. After all cities have Local Happiness equal to their Population, any remainder is distributed deck-of-cards style in order of highest to lowest Population.
How is Local City Happiness determined?

The calculation of Unhappiness from Needs is done by comparing a City's yield outputs per population to certain reference values, the Needs Thresholds. These values are based on the global median of yield outputs per population (i.e. the value of yield output per population that is exceeded by exactly 50% of cities worldwide). Only Cities with a population of at least 3 are considered when calculating the median, softening Unhappiness in the very early game. The Needs Thresholds are modified by a number of Needs Modifiers in each City. A positive Need Modifier makes it harder to reach the threshold and might therefore increase local Unhappiness, while a negative one might reduce it. The following modifiers are always applied:[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Capital Status[ENDCOLOR]: The Needs Thresholds of the Capital are increased by 25%.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_NEGATIVE_TEXT]Empire Size[ENDCOLOR]: Each City in your Empire (excluding the Capital and Puppet Cities) increases the Needs Thresholds in every City by 5%. Additionally, every eight Citizens in your Empire (excluding Citizens in Puppet Cities) increase them by 1%.[NEWLINE] [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Difficulty Level[ENDCOLOR]: On the Settler and Chieftain difficulties, Needs Thresholds are reduced for human players. On Difficulty Levels above Chieftain, no modifiers are applied.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Brazil's Carnival ability also reduces Needs Thresholds in all Cities by 50%. In addition, the Processes that convert Production into some other yield provide a reduction of the respective Need Threshold equal to the conversion rate (which can be increased using Power Plants), e.g. Farming converts 25% of Production into Food and decreases the Distress Need Threshold by 25%.

In Puppet Cities, special rules for Happiness and Unhappiness apply. Every 4 citizens in a Puppet City generate 1 Unhappiness. The only other possible source of Unhappiness in a Puppet City is Urbanization, which is calculated the same way as in other cities. In a Puppet City, you cannot control the assigment of specialists and therefore cannot counteract Urbanization unless you annex the city. Puppet Cities don't produce any local Happiness, and they follow their own rules for growth, independent of the Happiness system. The Unhappiness generated by Puppet Cities therefore only makes a difference at the empire level.
What causes Unhappiness in Puppet Cities?

Cities that are in Resistance or being Razed don't generate any Local Happiness. Instead, they generate Unhappiness equal to the city's population. This can massively decrease the Approval Rating of your empire.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Occupied Cities also don't produce any Happiness. They generate Unhappiness equal to the city's population, to which the regular Unhappiness from Urbanization is added.
What causes Unhappiness in Occupied and Resisting Cities?
The ruin contains relics that grant Golden Age Points.
The ruin contains supplies that grant Production to your nearest city.
The ruin contains settlers that grant free Tiles to your nearest city.

A number of mouse and keyboard shortcuts are available in Vox Populi to streamline many tasks! See [COLOR_GREEN]{TXT_KEY_TOPIC_SHORTCUT_WORLD_VIEW}[ENDCOLOR] for shortcuts pertaining to unit control in the main map view. See [COLOR_GREEN]{TXT_KEY_TOPIC_SHORTCUT_CITY_VIEW}[ENDCOLOR] for shortcuts related to building construction and city management.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Building Construction Modifiers:[ENDCOLOR] While left-clicking a building will place it at the bottom of the current cities construction queue, other actions can be accomplished with the use of modifier keys.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Insert Top[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]CTRL+LCLICK[ENDCOLOR] an item to add it to the top of the current cities construction queue.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Replace[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+LCLICK[ENDCOLOR] an item to replace the current cities construction queue with this item.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Repeat[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]ALT+LCLICK[ENDCOLOR] an item to repeat production of that item.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Insert Bottom All[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+ALT+LCLICK[ENDCOLOR] an item to add it to the bottom of every eligible cities construction queues.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Insert Top All[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+CTRL+LCLICK[ENDCOLOR] an item to add it to the top of every eligible owned cities construction queues.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Invest All[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+LCLICK[ENDCOLOR] a buildings invest button to invest in every copy of this building in any cities active construction queue.[NEWLINE]
[NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Citizen Management Modifiers:[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Set Yield Focus All[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+LCLICK[ENDCOLOR] a focus type to have all cities emphasize the production of that yield type.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Special Movement Actions:[ENDCOLOR] Most special movement actions such as rebasing can be executed by selecting the unit and [COLOR_YELLOW]right-clicking[ENDCOLOR] on a valid destination tile.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Airlift[ENDCOLOR]: With a land unit eligible to airlift selected, right click on an eligible airlift destination tile to airlift.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Change Home City[ENDCOLOR]: With a trade unit selected, right click on a city to change home city.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Change Port[ENDCOLOR]: With a Great Admiral in a city selected, right click on a coastal city to change port.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Rebase[ENDCOLOR]: With an air unit selected, right click on an eligible airlift destination tile to perform an airlift action.[NEWLINE]
[NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Move and Act Orders:[ENDCOLOR] [COLOR_YELLOW]CTRL+RCLICK[ENDCOLOR] issues a 'Move and Act' order, instructing a unit to move to the destination tile then perform their action.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Archaeologists[ENDCOLOR]: Archeological Dig.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Combat Units[ENDCOLOR]: Alert/Fortify Mode.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Diplomatic Units[ENDCOLOR]: Conduct Diplomatic Mission.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Great People[ENDCOLOR]: Construct Tile Improvement.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Inquisitors[ENDCOLOR]: Remove Heresy.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Missionaries[ENDCOLOR]: Spread Religion.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Workers/Workboats[ENDCOLOR]: Repair/Improve Resources.[NEWLINE]
[NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Queued Movement:[ENDCOLOR] Issue move orders with [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+RCLICK[ENDCOLOR] to create waypoints.[NEWLINE]
[NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Aircraft Group Commands:[ENDCOLOR] With an aircraft unit selected, modifier keys can be used to issue commands to all aircraft of the same type in the same airbase.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Massed Forward Rebase[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+RCLICK[ENDCOLOR] on an airbase will move all aircraft to that airbase until no more slots are available or all aircraft have rebased. Higher HP aircraft are prioritized, with ties broken by unit level.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Massed Fallback Rebase[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]ALT+RCLICK[ENDCOLOR] on an airbase will move all damaged aircraft to target airbase until no more slots are available or all aircraft have rebased. Lower HP aircraft are prioritized.[NEWLINE] [ICON_BULLET][COLOR_CYAN]Massed Strike Mode[ENDCOLOR]: [COLOR_YELLOW]SHIFT+RCLICK[ENDCOLOR] on an enemy will air strike the unit on the target hex until all aircraft have attacked or the target is dead. Attack order prioritizes higher HP aircraft, with ties being broken by unit level. Aircraft that can attack twice will do so before the next aircraft begins attacking.[NEWLINE]

[COLOR_CYAN]Special Ability: Establish Embassy[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]You can move a Great Diplomat to a City-State and construct an Embassy on a land tile. This is only possible if no other Embassy has already been established in the City-State. Each Embassy gives 1 additional vote in the World Congress. Establishing an Embassy consumes the Great Diplomat.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_CYAN]Special Ability: Conduct Diplomatic Mission[ENDCOLOR][NEWLINE]You can use a Great Diplomat in the territory of a City-State to conduct a Diplomatic Mission. You will get a large amount of influence with the City-State, and the influence of all other civilizations will decrease by the same amount. In addition, you will permanently get 1 Paper. This action consumes the Great Diplomat.

Civil Servants generate a variety of yields as well as points towards Great Diplomats. These units are essential if you are trying to win a Diplomatic Victory, or would like to earn a few more City-State alliances.

A civilization's World Map details every island, ocean, Natural Wonder and civilization that a civilization's explorers have discovered and charted. The trade of a civilization's World Map is available upon the discovery of Military Science, and it will reveal every tile that civilization has explored. World Maps do not provide contact with foreign civilizations, but it will chart their location and allow you to meet them! The value of a World Map goes up depending on how much undiscovered land that civilization can reveal to you: Natural Wonders and Resources are worth far more than vast, featureless oceans. World Maps can become expensive, so be sure to explore the world and cash in on the discovery income!
Once you have acquired the Replaceable Parts tech, you may sell your technological discoveries with another civ, as long as you have an Embassy in their capital.

A Vassalage Agreement is an agreement between two civilizations, where one civilization swears fealty to another civilization, becoming their vassal. In exchange for protection against other civilizations, the vassal surrenders their political power, including their right to become Leader of the World Congress and United Nations and ability to declare war (they follow their masters into war).

Vassals may only be obtained after entering the Medieval Era, and after a civilization has agreed to become your vassal. This agreement takes place in the Diplomacy Trade screen. There are two types of Vassalage: voluntary vassalage and capitulation.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Voluntary Vassalage is bought by the master during peacetime. Civilizations that are weak are more likely to surrender themselves as vassals, provided their new master is strong enough and close enough to protect them. Voluntary Vassalage is an agreement of choice only, and the vassal may choose to leave his master's service after a period of only 10 turns.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Capitulation, also known as "forceful vassalage," comes after a civilization has been defeated in war. In exchange for allowing them to live, the vassal agrees to surrender to their captor. Capitulation provides a number of more benefits to the master. The surrendering civilization agrees to forgive most negative diplomatic relations with the master and is forced to remain their vassal until a number of conditions are met. You can view these conditions in the Vassal Overview.

Vassalage may be ended between two civilizations in a variety of ways. The master may choose to declare war on their vassal, immediately ending vassalage between them. The master may choose to liberate their vassal, immediately ending the vassalage agreement (but also providing a very large diplomatic modifier with them)![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The vassal may also request independence from the master (after some conditions are met). The master always has the option of accepting or refusing their request for independence. In both events, the vassalage agreement is immediately ended, but if a master refuses a request for independence, war is immediately declared between the two civilizations.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Liberation of a vassal and requesting independence from a master are options available through the Vassal Overview. Consult this overview for eligibility requirements.

Vassalage comes with a variety of benefits for the master. The master receives free Open Borders with the vassal, and a free [ICON_DIPLOMAT] Diplomat in the Vassal's [ICON_CAPITAL] Capital, a percentage of the vassal's [ICON_RESEARCH] Science, [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, [ICON_PEACE] Faith. The master's [ICON_RELIGION] Religion and [ICON_TOURISM] Tourism to spread faster in their vassal's territory. The vassal contributes a small levy of units on each new era, the vassal is forced to adopt the Master's ideology, and the vassal is not eligible to host the World Congress or United Nations (unless the vassal founded it, in which case they will become the host of the World Congress until a new host is chosen).

Each vassal player in a team can be taxed at individual rates. This tax is applied through the Vassal Overview and is available immediately after the vassalage agreement is made. All taxes are applied at the start of a turn. Taxes are deducted from the vassal's [ICON_GOLD] Gross Gold Per Turn and are divided evenly amongst the civilizations in the master's team (if there are more than one player). Vassal taxes can be set in intervals of 5% starting from 0% and ending in 25%. Taxes may only be set after a set interval (notifications are sent out when vassal taxes are ready, and the Vassal Overview icon will show a number for the number of civilizations who have a pending tax change).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Heavily taxing a civilization will make them more likely to hate you and rebel against you when able to end vassalage.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Corporations[ENDCOLOR] are one of the new gameplay elements added in Vox Populi. They can have a great impact on your empire's economic development, especially in the later part of a game.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Founding Corporations[ENDCOLOR]: There are seven distinct Corporations in the game, each of which becomes available once you have researched the Corporations Technology during the Modern Age. Each Corporation has a specific set of Resource Monopolies that it relies upon - if you do not have at least one of these Resource Monopolies, you will not be able to found the Corporation. Once these two requirements are met, you need to construct the 'Headquarters' of the Corporation in one of your Cities. These buildings are World Wonders, so only one player in the world may found each Corporation! Furthermore, once you have founded a Corporation, you cannot found another one, so make sure you like the one you pick![NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Building Corporate Offices[ENDCOLOR]: Once you have founded your Corporation, you can begin establishing Corporate Offices in each of your Cities. These buildings come with special bonuses similar to your Corporation's Headquarters, and are thus worthwhile to construct on their own. Most bonuses from Corporations scale with the number of Cities you own, so larger empires benefit greatly from founding a Corporation and building as many Offices as possible!

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Monopolies[ENDCOLOR] are one of the new gameplay elements added in Vox Populi.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Luxury Global Monopolies[ENDCOLOR]: the essence of the Monopoly system is expansion: as your empire expands throughout the game (either through combat or settlement), be on the lookout for Luxury Resources that you already have copies of. As you collect more and more copies of the same Luxury Resources, the percentage of global resources you control goes up. If this value goes over 50% (i.e. you control more than 50% of the world's supply of any resource), you gain a Global Monopoly over that Resource. Each Global Monopoly has a unique bonus - some grant additional yields to your tiles, whereas others boost City yields by a set percentage (see the Resource section of the Civilopedia for details).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Strategic Global Monopolies[ENDCOLOR]: Strategic Resources operate the same way as Luxury Resources with regards to Monopolies, with one major exception. Due to the vast abundance of these resources, a true 50% Monopoly can be quite difficult. As a result, Strategic Resources have two tiers: 'Strategic' Monopolies and 'True' Monopolies. Strategic Monopolies occur at 25%, and generate special combat bonuses (such as increased health regeneration or increase defense). True Monopolies occur at 50% and, like Luxury Monopolies, they generate bonuses to City and/or tile yields.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Resource Monopolies are also required to found a [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Corporation[ENDCOLOR]. Each Corporation has a specific set of Resource Monopolies that it relies upon - if you do not have at least one of these Resource Monopolies, you will not be able to found the Corporation. For each Luxury and Strategic Resource, you can check the percentage of global resources you control in the "Corporations and Monopolies" screen.

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Corporation Types[ENDCOLOR]: there are seven Corporations available in Vox Populi. Each of these can only be constructed once (and only one per player), so choose wisely! For more on this, see the [COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Corporations[ENDCOLOR] Tab of the Civilopedia.
How do I spread my Corporation?

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Spreading your Corporation[ENDCOLOR] to foreign cities is an essential element of reaping the most benefit from your Corporation.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Active Spread: Corporations actively spread their influence via owned Trade Routes, but only if the origin City (your City) has a Corporate Office in it. If your City has a Corporate Office, and you send a Trade Route from that City to a foreign City, a Corporate 'Franchise' will be built in that foreign City when the Trade Route completes. There is also a random chance (~5%) that a Franchise will be created in a nearby Foreign city each turn, if you are currently trading with that Civilization. You can only spread your Corporation to each foreign City once, and you cannot have more Franchises than the maximum number of Trade Routes you can support.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Passive Spread: Corporations passively spread their influence via foreign Trade Routes, but only if the destination City (your City) has a Corporate Office in it. If your City has a Corporate Office, and another player sends a Trade Route to that City from one of their Cities, a Corporate 'Franchise' will be built in the foreign City when their Trade Route completes. Your Corporation can only spread to each foreign City once.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Benefits of Spreading Your Corporation[ENDCOLOR]: As listed in the details of each Corporation, the spread of your Corporation to foreign cities has a direct impact on the productivity of your Corporate Offices. For every 'Franchise' of your Corporation in a foreign City, your Corporate Offices gain unique bonuses, be it additional City yields, free resources, or improved Trade Route yields. Furthermore, many Corporations gain additional bonuses if you send Trade Routes to foreign Cities that already have your Corporation in them. Make sure to study the details of your Corporation once you have founded it so that you can maximize your benefit![NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]Managing your Corporation[ENDCOLOR]: As your Corporation grows, it can be hard to keep up with where you have Franchises, and where you have Offices. Never fear! In the Economic Overview panel, you can find detailed information on your Corporation in the bottom-left corner. There, you can see the total number of Offices and Corporations you currently control, as well as drop-down lists of the locations of all Corporate Offices and Franchises, as well as the size of foreign Corporations. In addition to these elements, you can also find information about your Corporation while choosing a destination for your Trade Routes. Each City with a Franchise in it is clearly indicated.
How do I spread my Corporation?

许多产出，尤其是来自政策、信仰和建筑的产出，表明它们[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]''与时代同步扩展''[ENDCOLOR]。这意味着，随着游戏的进展，指示的产量值会根据当前时代以线性方式增加：[NEWLINE]古代和古典时代的 1x。[NEWLINE]中世纪时期的 2 倍。[NEWLINE]文艺复兴时期的 3 倍。[NEWLINE]工业时代的 4 倍。[NEWLINE]现代时代的 5 倍。[NEWLINE]原子时代的 6 倍。[NEWLINE]信息时代的 7 倍。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]在像韩国这样的特殊情况下，他们可能会使用奇数时代进行缩放，或者在缩放之前跳过一个时代并遵循基于当前时代的格式，例如：[NEWLINE]古代/古典时代的 1x。[NEWLINE]中世纪/文艺复兴时期的 2 倍。[NEWLINE]工业/现代时代的 3 倍。[NEWLINE]原子/信息时代的 4 倍。
什么是收益率随时代的变化？
城邦大使馆是 Vox Populi 中获得世界大会代表的另一种方法。要在城邦建立大使馆，请将一位伟大外交官移动到城邦的一块土地上，然后选择“建立大使馆”。大使馆在世界大会上额外授予 1 名代表。在每个城邦中，一个文明只能设立一个大使馆，所以要快。当一个文明被征服时，其所有城邦大使馆都会转移到征服的文明。

附庸协议是两个文明之间的协议，其中一个文明宣誓效忠另一个文明，成为其附庸。为了换取对其他文明的保护，封臣放弃了他们的政治权力，包括他们成为世界大会和联合国领导人的权利以及宣战的能力（他们跟随他们的主人参战）。

封臣只有在进入中世纪时代并且某个文明同意成为你的封臣后才能获得。该协议发生在外交贸易屏幕中。附庸有两种类型：自愿附庸和投降。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]自愿附庸是主人在平时购买的。弱小的文明更有可能投降为附庸，只要它们的新主人足够强大并且足够接近来保护它们。自愿附庸只是一种选择协议，附庸可以选择在仅仅 10 个回合后离开主人的服务。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]投降，也被称为“强力附庸”，是在一个文明在战争中被击败之后发生的。作为允许他们生存的交换条件，封臣同意向俘虏他们的人投降。投降为主人提供了许多更多的好处。投降的文明同意宽恕与主人的大多数负面外交关系，并被迫继续担任他们的附庸，直到满足一些条件。您可以在附庸概述中查看这些条件。

两个文明之间的附庸关系可以通过多种方式结束。主人可以选择向他们的封臣宣战，立即结束他们之间的封臣关系。主人可能会选择解放他们的封臣，立即结束封臣协议（但也为他们提供了一个非常大的外交修正）！[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]封臣也可以请求独立于主人（在满足某些条件后）。主人总是可以选择接受或拒绝他们的独立请求。在这两种情况下，附庸协议都会立即终止，但如果主人拒绝独立请求，两个文明之间就会立即宣战。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]解放封臣和请求脱离主人独立是通过封臣概述提供的选项。请参阅此概述以了解资格要求。

封臣为主人带来了多种好处。主人与附庸获得免费的开放边界，并获得免费的[ICON_DIPLOMAT]附庸国的外交官[ICON_CAPITAL]资本，占封臣资本的百分比[ICON_RESEARCH]科学，[ICON_CULTURE]文化，[ICON_PEACE]信仰。大师的[ICON_RELIGION]宗教和[ICON_TOURISM]旅游业在其附庸国领土上传播得更快。封臣在每个新时代贡献少量单位，封臣被迫采用主人的意识形态，并且封臣没有资格主办世界大会或联合国（除非封臣创立了它，在这种情况下，他们将成为世界大会的东道主，直到选择新的东道主）。

团队中的每个附庸玩家都可以按个人税率纳税。该税通过附庸概览适用，并在附庸协议签订后立即可用。所有税费均在回合开始时适用。税收从封臣身上扣除[ICON_GOLD]每回合的总金币在大师团队中的文明之间平均分配（如果有超过一名玩家）。封臣税可以以 5% 为间隔设置，从 0% 开始，到 25% 结束。税收只能在设定的时间间隔后设置（当附庸税收准备就绪时会发出通知，并且附庸概述图标将显示有待处理税收更改的文明数量）。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]对一个文明征收重税将使他们在能够结束附庸时更有可能仇恨你并反抗你。

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]企业[ENDCOLOR]是 Vox Populi 中添加的新游戏元素之一。它们可以对帝国的经济发展产生巨大影响，尤其是在游戏的后期。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]创始公司[ENDCOLOR]：游戏中有七个不同的公司，一旦您研究了现代的公司技术，每个公司都将可用。每个公司都有一组它所依赖的特定资源垄断——如果您没有至少一个这些资源垄断，您将无法找到该公司。一旦满足这两个要求，您就需要在您的城市之一建造公司的“总部”。这些建筑都是世界奇迹，因此世界上只有一名玩家可以找到每个公司！此外，一旦您创建了一家公司，您就无法再创建另一家公司，因此请确保您喜欢您选择的一家！[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]建设公司办公室[ENDCOLOR]：一旦您成立了公司，您就可以开始在每个城市建立公司办事处。这些建筑物具有与您的公司总部类似的特殊奖励，因此值得自行建造。大多数公司的奖金都会随着您拥有的城市数量而增加，因此较大的帝国可以从建立公司和建造尽可能多的办事处中受益匪浅！

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]垄断[ENDCOLOR]是 Vox Populi 中添加的新游戏元素之一。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]奢侈品全球垄断[ENDCOLOR]：大富翁系统的本质是扩张：随着你的帝国在整个游戏中扩张（通过战斗或结算），请留意你已经拥有副本的豪华资源。当您收集越来越多的相同豪华资源副本时，您控制的全球资源的百分比就会上升。如果该值超过 50%（即您控制了世界上任何资源供应的 50% 以上），您就获得了该资源的全球垄断权。每个全球垄断都有独特的奖励 - 有些会给你的图块带来额外的收益，而另一些则以设定的百分比提高城市收益（有关详细信息，请参阅文明百科的资源部分）。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]战略性全球垄断[ENDCOLOR]：在垄断方面，战略资源的运作方式与奢侈品资源相同，但有一个重大例外。由于这些资源极其丰富，真正的 50% 垄断可能相当困难。因此，战略资源有两个层次：“战略”垄断和“真正”垄断。战略垄断发生率为 25%，并产生特殊的战斗奖励（例如增加生命恢复或增加防御）。真正的垄断发生率为 50%，并且与豪华垄断一样，它们会为城市和/或瓷砖产量带来奖金。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]资源垄断也需要建立[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]公司[ENDCOLOR]。每个公司都有一组它所依赖的特定资源垄断——如果您没有至少一个这些资源垄断，您将无法找到该公司。对于每种奢侈品和战略资源，您可以在“公司和垄断”屏幕中查看您控制的全球资源的百分比。
[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]公司类型[ENDCOLOR]：Vox Populi 中有 7 个公司。每一个都只能建造一次（每个玩家只能建造一个），所以请明智地选择！有关这方面的更多信息，请参阅[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]企业[ENDCOLOR]文明百科的选项卡。

[COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]传播您的公司[ENDCOLOR]到外国城市是从您的公司获得最大利益的重要因素。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]主动传播：公司通过拥有的贸易路线积极传播其影响力，但前提是起源城市（您的城市）在其中设有公司办事处。如果您的城市有一个公司办事处，并且您从该城市发送一条贸易路线到外国城市，则当贸易路线完成时，将在该外国城市建立企业“特许经营权”。如果您当前正在与该文明进行交易，则每轮都有随机机会（~5%）在附近的外国城市创建特许经营权。你只能将你的公司扩展到每个外国城市一次，并且你拥有的特许经营权不能超过你可以支持的贸易路线的最大数量。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]被动传播：公司通过对外贸易路线被动传播其影响力，但前提是目的地城市（您的城市）在其中设有公司办事处。如果您的城市有一个公司办公室，并且另一个玩家从他们的一个城市向该城市发送一条贸易路线，那么当他们的贸易路线完成时，将在外国城市建立一个公司“特许经营权”。你的公司只能扩展到每个外国城市一次。[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]扩展公司的好处[ENDCOLOR]：正如每个公司的详细信息所列出的那样，您的公司在国外城市的分布对您公司办事处的生产力有直接的影响。对于您的公司在外国城市的每一个“特许经营权”，您的公司办事处都会获得独特的奖励，无论是额外的城市收益、免费资源还是提高的贸易路线收益。此外，如果您将贸易路线发送到已经有您的公司的外国城市，许多公司会获得额外的奖金。一旦你成立了你的公司，一定要研究它的细节，这样你才能最大化你的利益！[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][COLOR_POSITIVE_TEXT]管理您的公司[ENDCOLOR]：随着您的公司不断发展，可能很难跟上您拥有特许经营权和办事处的情况。永远不要害怕！在经济概览面板中，您可以在左下角找到有关您公司的详细信息。在那里，您可以看到您当前控制的办事处和公司总数，以及所有公司办事处和特许经营权位置的下拉列表，以及外国公司的规模。除了这些元素之外，您还可以在选择贸易路线的目的地时找到有关您的公司的信息。每个拥有特许经营权的城市都有明确的指示。
